notice: Curated source metadata and summaries for a demo. This is not a complete legal text, legal opinion, or authorisation.

sources.title: CMA licensing checklists
sources.summary: The CMA publishes separate licensing checklists for market-intermediary categories. Its page says the checklists are summaries and the underlying regulations are conclusive.
sources.limitation: A checklist is not a licence and does not determine VYRA's classification.

sources.authority: Parliament of Kenya / Capital Markets Authority
sources.title: Capital Markets (Collective Investment Schemes) Regulations, 2023
sources.summary: The regulations state that a person shall not operate an intermediary service platform without an ISPP licence, and that marketing and distribution of schemes from multiple fund managers requires CMA approval.
sources.limitation: The current consolidated and transitional position, and the exact VYRA journey, need qualified Kenyan counsel and CMA confirmation.

sources.authority: National Treasury / Central Bank of Kenya / Capital Markets Authority
sources.title: Virtual Asset Service Providers Regulations, 2026 (Legal Notice 134 of 2026)
provisions: Regulation 4: application in or from Kenya
sources.summary: The regulations apply to persons offering virtual-asset services in or from Kenya. Targeting local consumers or deriving economic benefit/income from Kenya can establish this connection even without physical presence. Licensing and promotion obligations are activity-specific.
sources.limitation: Exact service category, regulator, transitional provisions and VYRA's role require current legal review.

sources.authority: Central Bank of Kenya and Capital Markets Authority
sources.title: Public notice: gazettement of the VASP Regulations, 2026
sources.summary: The joint notice says persons providing or intending to provide virtual-asset services must apply to the relevant regulator under the applicable service category.
sources.limitation: The notice does not confer a licence or appointment on VYRA.

sources.title: CMA Regulatory Sandbox eligibility
sources.summary: The CMA describes eligibility for a Kenyan-incorporated company or a firm licensed by an equivalent securities regulator, intending to offer an innovative solution in Kenya. The page excludes products, services or models already clearly addressed under existing laws.
sources.limitation: A sandbox is a supervised testing route, not a general exemption or automatic permission.
